source_text:
Τούτοις τοῖς ἀνδράσιν ὁσίως πολιτευσαμένοις συνηθροίσθη πολὺ πλῆθος ἐκλεκτῶν, οἵτινες πολλαῖς αἰκίαις καὶ βασάνοις διὰ ζῆλος παθόντες ὑπόδειγμα κάλλιστον ἐγένοντο ἐν ἡμῖν.
διὰ ζῆλος διωχθεῖσαι γυναῖκες Δαναΐδες καὶ Δίρκαι, αἰκίσματα δεινὰ καὶ ἀνόσια παθοῦσαι, ἐπὶ τὸν τῆς πίστεως βέβαιον δρόμον κατήντησαν καὶ ἔλαβον γέρας γενναῖον αἱ ἀσθενεῖς τῷ σώματι.
ζῆλος ἀπηλλοτρίωσεν γαμετὰς ἀνδρῶν καὶ ἠλλοίωσεν τὸ ῥηθὲν ὑπὸ τοῦ πατρὸς ἡμῶν Ἀδάμ: Τοῦτο νῦν ὀστοῦν ἐκ τῶν ὀστέων μου καὶ σὰρξ ἐκ τῆς σαρκός μου.
ζῆλος καὶ ἔρις πόλεις μεγάλας κατέστρεψεν καὶ ἔθνη μεγάλα ἐξερίζωσεν.
orientation: Clement is piling up examples of the harm envy has done, moving from the apostles to other faithful sufferers and to the destructive power of envy in families and cities.
pass_a_gloss: To these men who conducted themselves holily, a great multitude of the elect was gathered together, who, having suffered many outrages and tortures because of envy, became a most beautiful example among us. Because of envy, women were persecuted—the Danaids and Dircae, having suffered terrible and unholy outrages, they reached the sure course of the faith and received a noble prize, they who were weak in body. Envy estranged wives from husbands and changed what was said by our father Adam: This now is bone from my bones and flesh from my flesh. Envy and faction overturned great cities and rooted out great nations.

choices.why: The source names are mythological allusions; keeping the Greek names preserves the reference without inventing an interpretation.

choices.term: ἐπὶ τὸν τῆς πίστεως βέβαιον δρόμον κατήντησαν
choices.english: they reached the sure course of the faith
choices.why: δρόμος is a racecourse metaphor; 'sure course' keeps the athletic image and the adjective βέβαιον as 'sure' rather than 'firm' to avoid a fixed-ministry echo.
rejected: they arrived at the firm path of faith
they attained the steadfast race of faith

choices.why: γέρας is a prize of honor, and γενναῖον means noble; 'noble prize' keeps both the honorific and the quality.

choices.english: they who were weak in body
choices.why: The phrase is appositional and emphasizes the paradox; keeping it as a separate clause preserves the source's word order and emphasis.
γαμετὰς ἀνδρῶν is literally 'wives of husbands'; 'wives from husbands' captures the alienation force of ἀπηλλοτρίωσεν.
rejected: Envy alienated married women from their husbands
Envy made wives strangers to their husbands

choices.why: ἐκριζόω is literally 'to root out'; the agricultural metaphor is vivid and should be kept.

bible_refs.note: Τοῦτο νῦν ὀστοῦν ἐκ τῶν ὀστέων μου καὶ σὰρξ ἐκ τῆς σαρκός μου

pass_b_english: A great multitude of the elect gathered around these men who had conducted themselves in holiness. Because of envy they suffered many outrages and tortures, and among us they became a most beautiful example.
Because of envy women were persecuted as Danaids and Dircae. They suffered terrible and unholy torments, yet they finished the race of faith, and they who were weak in body received a noble prize.
Envy estranged wives from husbands and changed what our father Adam said: “This now is bone of my bones and flesh of my flesh” (Genesis 2:23).
Envy and faction overthrew great cities and rooted out great nations.

problems.why: Glossary requires 'faction' for ἔρις in this work's context; 'strife' is banned per ζῆλος/ἔρις as root causes of Corinthian trouble.
problems.fix: Envy and faction overthrew great cities and rooted out great nations.

edits.old: Envy and strife overthrew great cities and rooted out great nations.
edits.new: Envy and faction overthrew great cities and rooted out great nations.

fixed: Changed 'strife' to 'faction' in the English and gloss to match the glossary requirement for ἔρις.

problems.quote: women were persecuted as Danaids and Dircae
problems.source_quote: διὰ ζῆλος διωχθεῖσαι γυναῖκες Δαναΐδες καὶ Δίρκαι
problems.why: Greek says women 'persecuted by envy' who 'were Danaids and Dircae', not 'persecuted as'. These are proper names of persecuted women, not comparisons.
problems.fix: women persecuted by envy, the Danaids and Dircae
problems.ruling: Δαναΐδες καὶ Δίρκαι are appositional IDs of the persecuted women, not similes; 'as' misleads readers into thinking they are mere comparisons.

edits.old: Because of envy, women were persecuted as Danaids and Dircae.
edits.new: Because of envy, women were persecuted—the Danaids and Dircae.

fixed: The edit changes 'persecuted as' to 'persecuted—the Danaids and Dircae', which correctly identifies Danaids and Dircae as the women who were persecuted, not as a comparison.

problems.quote: women were persecuted—the Danaids and Dircae
problems.why: Greek uses nominative, not accusative: these women ARE the Danaids and Dircae, not separate from them.
problems.fix: women were persecuted, Danaids and Dircae,
problems.ruling: Nominatives γυναῖκες Δαναΐδες καὶ Δίρκαι are in apposition: the women ARE the Danaids and Dircae, not a separate group.

edits.old: Because of envy, women were persecuted—the Danaids and Dircae.
edits.new: Because of envy, women were persecuted, Danaids and Dircae,

problems.why: Reader may not recognize these all refer to the same group.
Greek terms may differ, but reader sees varying English pairs.
problems.fix: Note if these translate distinct Greek terms or are stylistic variation.

problems.quote: they reached the sure course of the faith
problems.why: 'Sure course' is meaningless; should be 'finished the course' or 'completed the race.'
problems.fix: Revise to: 'they finished the race of faith.'

problems.why: Used interchangeably for people and groups; reader may wonder if 'the elect' is a distinct group from 'the elect of God'.
problems.fix: Standardize to 'the elect of God' or clarify it refers to all believers.

edits.old: they reached the sure course of the faith
edits.new: they finished the race of faith

fixed: The glossary problems about 'the elect of God' and 'envy and spite' do not appear in the provided English text; the English uses 'the elect' and 'envy and faction', which are consistent with the glossary and source.
The mistranslation 'they reached the sure course of the faith' was corrected to 'they finished the race of faith'.

problems.why: The core problem is rendered with several different nouns; readers may miss that all refer to the same schism.
problems.fix: Use 'faction' or 'division' consistently for the same concept.

edits.old: Because of envy women were persecuted, Danaids and Dircae.
edits.new: Because of envy women were persecuted—Danaids and Dircae.

fixed: The glossary issue about 'faction' is not a translation error in this passage; the English uses 'faction' consistently for the source term in the final sentence, and no change is needed here.

problems.why: Key concept rendered inconsistently; reader may miss that all refer to the same group.
problems.fix: Standardize to 'the elect' or 'the elect of God' throughout.

edits.old: A great multitude of the elect gathered around these men
edits.new: A great multitude of the elect of God gathered around these men

fixed: The English already uses 'the elect' consistently; the confirmed problem suggests standardizing to 'the elect' or 'the elect of God'. I added 'of God' to the first occurrence to make the referent explicit, matching the source's 'ἐκλεκτῶν' in context of God's chosen people.

polish.changed: Clarified the opening sentence by naming the subject of the gathering, smoothed sentence rhythm, and kept every claim and quotation intact.
Clarified that the elect are the same group throughout, made the mythological references read as titles applied to the persecuted women, and smoothed sentence rhythm for reading aloud.

notes.why: Key concept rendered inconsistently; reader may miss that all refer to the same group.
notes.fix: Standardize to 'the elect' or 'the elect of God' throughout.

notes.why: Mythological figures/titles with no context; reader cannot identify them.
notes.fix: Add a note: 'Legendary or symbolic women, possibly Christian martyrs.'

last_rejected.quote: They suffered many outrages and tortures because of envy, and among us they became a most beautiful example.
last_rejected.source_quote: οἵτινες πολλαῖς αἰκίαις καὶ βασάνοις διὰ ζῆλος παθόντες ὑπόδειγμα κάλλιστον ἐγένοντο ἐν ἡμῖν
last_rejected.why: English hides that the elect suffered: 'they suffered' should attach to 'a great multitude of the elect', not the men.
last_rejected.fix: To these men who conducted themselves in holiness a great multitude of the elect was gathered, who suffered many outrages and tortures because of envy and became a most beautiful example among us.
last_rejected.ruling: οἵτινες refers back to πολὺ πλῆθος ἐκλεκτῶν; English 'They' correctly points to the elect multitude.

last_rejected.quote: Because of envy, women were persecuted, Danaids and Dircae
last_rejected.source_quote: διὰ ζῆλος διωχθεῖσαι γυναῖκες Δαναΐδες καὶ Δίρκαι
last_rejected.why: Passive 'were persecuted' obscures agency; participles show women actively enduring persecution, not receiving it.
last_rejected.fix: Because of envy women suffered persecution, the Danaids and Dircae,
last_rejected.ruling: διωχθεῖσαι is aorist passive participle 'having been persecuted'; English passive correctly renders it.
